Path('docs/decisions/0009-ticket-assignment.md').write_text('''# 9. Ticket assignment

Status: Accepted

## Context

Operators need to assign active tickets and see ownership in the API and command line.

## Decision

Tickets carry a nullable assignee. Older data files without the field load with null, retaining data file version 1.
Assignment uses a dedicated PUT endpoint, only for open and in-progress tickets. The store audits each actual change
and enqueues a notification for each new assignment, with a key based on the audit sequence so repeated assignments
are independently delivered even while earlier notifications wait. Unassignment sends no notification.

Assignee is appended after the four established raw CLI columns, preserving weekly report positions. Listing filters
combine with AND, including the assignee filter; an empty assignee query selects null.

## Consequences

Existing files remain readable. Consumers of raw output can read ownership in column five while the existing report
continues to use the original four columns.
''')

p=Path('docs/api.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'''\n## Import tickets\n\n`POST /tickets/import` takes `{ "tickets": [...] }`, with up to 5000 objects in the same format as\n`POST /tickets`. An empty array succeeds. Each item uses the usual field validation, trimming and priority default.\nOn success the response is 201 with `{ "created": 2, "ids": ["T-0001", "T-0002"] }`, in input order.\nAn invalid item returns 400 in the usual error envelope, with the first invalid zero-based index in the message\n(for example, `tickets[1]: title must be a string`). The entire import is rejected without consuming ids,\nadding audit entries or enqueueing notifications. Each successful creation has its usual audit entry and requester\nnotification, with the actor from `X-Actor`.\n\nThe import body limit is the greater of `MAX_BODY_BYTES` and 16 MiB, to accommodate 5000 full-size ticket objects.\nOther routes retain `MAX_BODY_BYTES`. The batch is saved once, so imports do not rewrite the data file per ticket.\n''')
p=Path('README.md');p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('the largest request body accepted |','the largest request body accepted (imports allow at least 16 MiB) |'))
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'| 10 | [Atomic ticket imports](0010-atomic-ticket-imports.md) | Accepted |\n')
Path('docs/decisions/0010-atomic-ticket-imports.md').write_text('''# 10. Atomic ticket imports

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Migration from the old tracker needs up to 5000 tickets per request, within ten seconds. Saving the entire state
once per ticket would make large imports unnecessarily expensive.

## Decision

We validate all items in input order before changing the store. The store stages the batch with the same creation
logic as individual requests, then saves once and publishes the resulting state. Each ticket retains its own audit
entry and outbox event. Invalid items report their zero-based index. The import route accepts at least 16 MiB;
other routes retain their configured body limit.

## Consequences

Validation and persistence failures leave the live store unchanged. Imports use memory for a staged copy of state
and perform a single data-file write. Existing file formats and notification delivery remain compatible.
''')

p=Path('docs/api.md');s=p.read_text();s+='\nWith `DUE_TIMES=on`, all ticket responses include `due`, an ISO UTC time fixed at creation. `GET /tickets?overdue=true` selects only open and in-progress tickets strictly past that time, combined with other filters before pagination. `overdue=false` applies no additional filter; other values return 400. With the flag off, due is omitted and the overdue parameter is ignored as before.\n';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/operations.md');s=p.read_text();s+='''
## Due-time rollout and rollback

Back up DATA_FILE before deployment. Start the new release with DUE_TIMES unset. At startup it backfills missing due times from each ticket's creation time and priority, saves the whole data file atomically, and only then accepts requests. It preserves existing deadlines, audit entries and notifications. New tickets also receive persisted deadlines while the flag is off. Review the file for due values before restarting with DUE_TIMES=on. A failed backfill save prevents startup, so no unsaved deadlines are served.

Set RESPONSE_HOURS_URGENT, RESPONSE_HOURS_HIGH, RESPONSE_HOURS_NORMAL and RESPONSE_HOURS_LOW before preparation to choose the response hours. Later changes affect new tickets only. Due times use elapsed hours in UTC, independent of daylight saving time.

For rollback, stop this release and start 1.4.0 on the same data file. Its version stays 1; due is an additive ticket field and existing record shapes and enums stay unchanged, so 1.4.0 can load every ticket. It ignores due and can discard it on its next save. Keep the backup if original deadlines must be restored after an old-release write; on a later upgrade, missing deadlines will be backfilled from the then-current priority and response settings. Stop the service before any manual restore and never run two writers against one data file.
''';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('CHANGELOG.md');p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('# Changelog', '# Changelog\n\n## 1.7.0 (2026-11-15)\n\n- Persist immutable due times with configurable response hours, backfill existing tickets before serving, and gate due output and overdue filtering behind DUE_TIMES=on. Keep the version 1 data format readable by 1.4.0.'))
p=Path('docs/decisions/0011-persisted-due-times.md');p.write_text('''# 11. Persisted due times

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Response promises must survive priority and configuration changes, and deployments need staged activation and rollback to 1.4.0.

## Decision

Store due as an optional additive ticket field in the existing version 1 document. Backfill missing values and save before serving. Compute new deadlines on creation, including imports, even while public output is disabled. Expose due and overdue selection only with DUE_TIMES=on. Preserve all existing audit and outbox semantics.

## Consequences

Operators can prepare the file before enabling the feature. Existing deadlines are never recomputed. The old reader accepts the document but may discard additive fields when saving; operators retain a backup for deadline-preserving rollback. Overdue filtering precedes pagination and uses the injected clock.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'\n| 11 | [Persisted due times](0011-persisted-due-times.md) | Accepted |\n')
